messages.author: 274786ec2f7eed2e
messages.subject: Regarding cluster size
parts:
Dear all,
I am perusing PhD on marine mammals as specifically dolphins.i have not used any statistical analysis before my PhD study for marine mammals. I am very new for Distance software. Regarding data analysis in software I do not understand the term "Cluster size". Is it number of animals in a single group or number of groups observed in transect? so you are requested to please clarify about this. 
Thanking you

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: {Disarmed} Re: [distance-sampling] Regarding cluster size
parts:
Yash

"Cluster size" refers to the number of individuals in a detected group.  Different species have different names for animal groups: fish occur in schools, dolphins in pods, wild dogs in packs.  In distance sampling literature we refer use the term "cluster" to apply to these situations.

Eric Rexstad
Senior Research Fellow, CREEM, Univ. of St Andrews, Charity SC013532
eric.r...@st-andrews.ac.uk
